newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish farmers on offensive over Russian beef deal.
newsitem.headline: Irish farmers on offensive over Russian beef deal.

text.p: The president of the Irish Farmers Association said on Thursday the country's policy on mad cow disease was in tatters following a government decision to stop exports of beef from three Irish counties to Russia.
Irish Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates signed an agreement with Russia stopping exports of beef to Russia from the counties of Cork, Tipperary and Monaghan from November 1.

Yates said Russia had threatened a complete ban on Irish beef because of fears that Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) could be transmitted to humans. Ireland instead accepted a selective agreement stopping exports from the three counties.
"Essentially I had no choice. It was...accept this level of regionalisation or there would be a total ban. It's a temporary setback and it's much better than the ban," Yates said.

But the agreement provoked fury among Irish farmers and opposition politicians, who said the agreement would damage confidence in Irish beef and encourage other countries to introduce selective bans on some Irish beef.
Irish Farmers Association President John Donnelly said immediate political action was needed to restore international confidence in the country's beef.
"Government policy on beef is now in tatters," Donnelly told Irish radio. "The concession that minister Yates made to the Russians does untold damage."
Ireland says its beef is safe to eat and it has strict policies to deal with BSE. The country has reported 153 occurences of BSE, including 40 in Cork, eight in Tipperary and five in Monaghan.
Russia is Ireland's biggest single beef export market.
